JUDGMENT
This petition is filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of M.V.Act, 1989 claiming compensation of Rs.30,00,000/ in respect of accidental injuries sustained by him in the Road Traffic Accident.

Basavegowda vs Rakshith A.R on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104850421/
1 2.

It is the case of the petitioner that, on 23.07.2021 at about 9.45 a.m he was riding his TVS XL Super Moped bearing Regn.No.KA54J5081 on the extreme left side of Bangalore Mangaluru NH75 road from Amruthur, slowly, carefully and by observing all traffic rules and regulations, and when he reached near Nelligee Circle, Bellur Hobli, Nagamangala Taluk, Mandya District, at that time a motor cycle bearing reg.no.KA01HW 5028 ridden by its rider at high sped in a rash and negligent manner dashed petitioner's motor cycle.
Due to the impact, he fell down on the road and sustained both bones fracture to his right leg.
immediately after the accident the petitioner was admitted to Adichunchanagiri hospital, B.G.Nagar and he underwent below knee amputation and stump closure to his right leg.
He has spent Rs.1,95,000/ towards medical, conveyance, food and nourishment charges and other expenses.
He is suffering from permanent disability as he is not able to do (SCCH12) 3 MVC No.217/2022 any work.

Prior to accident he was doing agriculture,
siriculture work and also he was dong milk vending business and earning Rs.20,000/ per month.
After the accident, he is not able to do any work and lost his entire earnings.
The injuries sustained have caused permanent disability.
The accident is solely due to rash and negligent riding of rider of motor cycle bearing reg.no.KA01HW5028.
The Bellur Police have registered case in Crime No.111/2021 for the offence p/u/s 279, 337 of IPC.
After investigation they have filed charge sheet against the opponent vehicle rider for the offence p/u/s 279 and 338 of IPC.
The respondent No.1 is the R.C owner and respondent no.2 is the insurer of opponent vehicle are liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
On all these grounds he prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.30,00,000/ with interest and costs in the above case.
3. On issuance of notice, respondent no.1 and 2 appeared through their respective counsel and have filed written statement separately.
Respondent no.1 contended that petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts.
Further he has denied the accident.
That this respondent was having valid licence and his vehicle has been insured and the policy was valid on the date of alleged accident.
The age, occupation, income and permanent disability of the petitioner are denied.

He stated that, no accident as alleged by the petitioner took place on 23.07.2021 that vehicle of this respondent has passed on the said road at the accident spot on that day, but no accident took place as alleged, but police have filed false case against this (SCCH12) 4 MVC No.217/2022 respondent.
They have summoned this respondent and he has produced himself with motor cycle along with relevant documents.
After inspection inspector gave clear certificate that motor vehicle of this respondent has not got any damage that could occur through accident.
Inspite of such report, due to some mistaken identity of some other vehicle police have filed false case against this respondent.
On all these grounds he prayed to dismiss the claim petition.
4. Respondent no.2 contended that petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts.
Further it has admitted the issuance of policy in respect of motor cycle bearing reg.no.KA01HW5028 in favour of 1 st respondent.

That the liability of this respondent if any, is subject to the validity of R.C,
F.C and permit of the vehicle and also the driving licence of the driver of the vehicles involved in the alleged accident and the terms and conditions of the insurance policy and the provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act ad Rules.

That it is not liable to indemnify the owner of the insured motor cycle or pay any compensation to the petitioner in the event of breach of policy conditions and violation of provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act.

That the accident if any was due to the negligence of the petitioner being the rider of motor cycle bearing reg.no.KA54J5081 and he was unmindful of the Basavegowda vs Rakshith A.R on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104850421/
2 traffic rules and movement of vehicles on road.

sentences.text: The petitioner has contributed higher degree of negligence of the alleged accident, but the police without proper investigation have registered the case against the rider of motor cycle bearing reg.no.KA01HW (SCCH12) 5 MVC No.217/2022 5028.

That the 1st respondent is the owner and he has insured the said vehicle with this respondent,
he has not personally informed about the same until this respondent received the summons from this Hon'ble tribunal and has not furnished the particulars of the policy as contemplated under section 134 C of the M.V.Act.
Further the police authorities have not complied the provision of Section 158(6) of M.V.Act.

That the petitioner being the rider of the motor cycle had no valid driving license to ride the said vehicle, he was not wearing helmet, while riding the moped and the rider of insured motor cycle bearing reg.no.KA01HW5028 had also no valid driving license to ride the same as on the date of alleged accident.
The owner of the insured motor cycle had knowingly and willfully entrusted the vehicle to a person, who had no valid driving license.
There was breach of terms and conditions of the insurance policy and violation of the provisions of motor vehicles act.

That if the owner of the insured motor cycle remains absent or fails to contest the case, this respondent my be permitted to defend the claim petition on all grounds under Section 170 of Motor Vehicles Act.

Further stated that, the amount claimed as compensation is baseless, speculative,
imaginary and exorbitant and this respondent is not liable to pay any compensation.

The age,
occupation, income and permanent disability of the petitioner are denied.
On all these grounds he prayed to dismiss the claim petition.

5. On the basis of above pleadings, my learned predecessors inoffice has framed following:
(SCCH12) 6 MVC No.217/2022 ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that the injuries shown in petition are sustained by him in a motor vehicle accident occurred on 23.07.2021 due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of motor cycle bearing reg.no.KA01 HW5028 when it hit his TVS XL Super Moped bearing Reg.No.KA54J 5081?
2. Whether the petitioner proves his age, occupation, income and permanent disability if any?
3. Whether the 2nd respondent proves that the rider of motor cycle bearing reg.no.KA01HW 5028 did not possess valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident?

4. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation? If so by whom and what is the quantum?
5. What Order or Award?
6. To prove his case, petitioner entered witness box and got examined as P.W.1.
Through him Ex.P.1 to P.12 documents are marked.
One Doctor Nagaraj B.N Orthopaedic Surgeon, SOADS is examined as P.W.2 and through him Ex.P.13 and 14 documents are marked.
Further one Medical Record Officer, Adichunchanagiri Hospital, B.G.Nagara,Mandya District is examined as P.W.3.
Through him Ex.P.15 to 18 documents are marked.
On the the hand, respondent no.1 is examined as R.W.1.
Through him Ex.R.1 and R2 are marked.
2 nd respondent has not led any evidence and respondent evidence is closed.

Basavegowda vs Rakshith A.R on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104850421/
3 7.
Heard learned counsel for both sides and perused records.
It is stated in the petition that petitioner was also travelling on another two wheeler bearing reg.no.KA54J5081.
According to petitioner, the accident took place due to sole negligence of the opponent insured vehicle rider.
To prove his case petitioner entered himself into witness box and got examined himself as P.W.1 and he has reiterated petition averments.

He produced FIR, first information, spot mahazar, IMV report, wound certificate, final report and discharge summary at Ex.P.1 to 9.
10.

As per the first information one D.Prasanna, who is the son of petitioner has given first information to Bellur police station stating that he was informed by one Naveen that father of first informant was travelling on Moped two wheeler on (SCCH12) 8 MVC No.217/2022 23.07.2021 at about 10.00 am and got accident through one two wheeler bearing reg.no.KA01HW5028 by which his father sustained injuries to his right leg and shifted to A.C.Giri hospital.
On receipt of such information this first informant went to the said hospital and found that his father sustained injuries to his right leg and was bleeding.
Then his father informed that aforesaid two wheeler rider came in rash and negligent manner and caused accident.
Therefore, this first informant requested the police to take action against the opponent insured vehicle rider.
On that first information Bellur police have registered Crime No.111/2021 against the rider of motor vehicle no.KA01HW5028 on 23.07.2021.
On the same day of the accident FIR is registered and there is no delay in filing the first information.
As per the spot panchanama it can be seen that, it is 28ft wide tar road and having footpath of 12ft wide and accident too place 3ft away from north side of the road.
There is also blood stain found on the road.
In the first information it is mentioned that on the right side of the two wheeler of the petitioner, opponent vehicle was hit.
11. In the cross examination of P.W.1 he stated that opponent vehicle came from backside and he has not seen the bike coming.
He stated that it was coming in high speed.
The suggestion that petitioner himself was in high speed as it was highway is denied.
He stated that he was 2ft away from the mud road.
There is rough sketch in the spot mahazar itself which shows that accident took place near the cross road in circle.
The opponent vehicle had allegedly come from Bengaluru (SCCH12) 9 MVC No.217/2022 side and as per the sketch the accident took place at the circle.

At that place, opponent Basavegowda vs Rakshith A.R on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104850421/
4 vehicle rider must have been more cautious while passing his vehicle near circle.

sentences.text: In the written statement of respondent no.1 stated that his vehicle passed on the said road on that day, but according to him no accident took place as alleged.
He stated that his vehicle was not involved in the accident, but false case is filed against him.
But in wound certificate it is mentioned that, alleged history of RTA hit by a racing vehicle around 9.45 am and it is hit and run case.
As per Ex.P.8 final report there is negligence on part of the insured vehicle rider.
It is also mentioned in the charge sheet that opponent vehicle rider has not answered to IMV notice issued U/s 133 of IMV Act.
It is also mentioned that, the said bike rider came by making high sound of the bike in rash and negligent manner caused accident and ran away from the spot.
Even in the discharge summary it is mentioned as case of RTA.

Though first respondent contended that his vehicle was not involved in the accident,
he has not produced any document to show that, his bike was not involved in the accident.
In the police intimation produced at Ex.P.17 also it is mentioned that, hit by racing bike.
Contrary to his evidence there is no evidence available in support of respondent no.1 Nothing is elicited in respect of negligence of petitioner in the cross examination of R.W.1.

Hence, in the opinion of this court on the basis of available evidence it is clear that rider of opponent vehicle bearing reg.no no.KA01HW 5028 was negligent in riding the (SCCH12) 10 MVC No.217/2022 two wheeler and caused accident to petitioner.
Accordingly I hold this issue in the Affirmative 12. ISSUE NO.2 : Respondent no.2 has disputed the age, occupation, income and permanent disability of the petitioner.
To prove his age petitioner produced his aadhaar card at Ex.P.10 which show that he was born on 01.01.1966.
As on the date of accident i.e., 23.07.2021 he was 55 years old.
In the final report age of the petitioner is mentioned as 59 years.
In the medical record also his age is mentioned as 59 years.
But, as per the aadhaar card which is issued on 06.05.2014, at an undisputed point of time, his age is 55 years at the time of accident.
There is contrary evidence to this fact from the respondent side.
Hence, the age mentioned in the aadhaar card considered for the purpose of this case and it is held that petitioner was aged 55 years at the time of accident.
13. Both the respondents have disputed the occupation of the petitioner.
In respect of occupation it is stated that, petitioner is an Agriculturist having Siriculture and milk vending business and was earning Rs.20,000/ per month.
But, no documents are produced to show his occupation or income.
Therefore, notional income has to be inferred.

In the case of Smt. Mariyamma and others V/s Suyambulingam.V. and another, MFA 7404/2014 dated 06.12.2022 the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has held that tribunal has to consider the provisions of Minimum Wages Act to decide notional income.

entities.text: Smt. Mariyamma and others V/s Suyambulingam.V. and another, MFA 7404/2014
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: But in the present case occupation is also not proved.

Therefore, in the opinion of this court, petitioner being resident of Honnenahalli, Bellur Hobli, Nagamangala Taluk, Mandya Dist and the accident took place in 2021,
having regard to the cost of living, if the income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.14,000/ per month the interest of justice would be met.

Hence, the income of the petitioner per month is considered as Rs.14,000/.
14.
To prove permanent disability, petitioner got examined doctor by name Nagaraj B.N as PW2.
The doctor has given evidence and stated that, petitioner sustained injuries in road traffic accident and sustained right leg open type III C compound fracture.

That he was treated in Adichunchunagiri Basavegowda vs Rakshith A.R on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104850421/
5 hospital and underwent below knee amputation and stump closure.

entities.text: Adichunchunagiri Basavegowda vs Rakshith A.R on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: That he cannot walk properly and stump is measuring 5 inches.
According to the doctor the disability is at 70%.
It is settled law that, doctor can only assess physical disability and cannot assess the functional disability having regard to avocation of the patient
. He is cross examined and denied material suggestions.
Petitioner being agriculturist suffered grievous injuries of fracture of right leg and it was amputed.
The said injury would come in the way of his occupation.
That he cannot do any normal work as he used to work before the accident.
Therefore, his functional disability affecting the occupation of the petitioner in the opinion of this court is held as 70%.
Accordingly I answer this issue Partly in the Affirmative.
(SCCH12) 12 MVC No.217/2022 15. ISSUE NO.3 : 2nd respondent contended that the rider of the two wheeler bearing reg.no.KA 01HW5028 was not having effective D.L at the time of accident.
But, there is no such charge in the final report against the accused.

Further, 2 nd respondent has not given any evidence in this regard to prove that the rider of the said vehicle had no D.L. That apart, 1 st respondent ridercum owner of the vehicle has furnished his driving licence at Ex.R.1.
That shows he was holding valid D.L as on the date of accident.
Therefore, this issue is not proved before this court.
Accordingly, I hold this Issue in the Negative.
16. ISSUE NO.4 :
In view of above reasons, injuries sustained by petitioner are due to the accident caused by the rider of the two wheeler bearing reg.no.KA01HW5028.
There is nexus between the injuries sustained by the petitioner and the accident.
Hence he is entitled to compensation at the hands of respondents.

The quantum of compensation is determined as under:
(i) For Pain and sufferings: The petitioner has sustained one grievous injury and he was in hospital from 23.07.2021 to 23.08.2021.
The records show that he underwent operation and amputation of right leg.
He was in hospital for one month with advice to take complete rest, continue medicine and to take follow up treatment.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Mohd Sabeer @ Shabir Hussain V/s Regional Manager U.P State Road Transport Corporation, Civil Appeal No.9070 9071 of 2022 dated 09.12.2022 has awarded Rs.2,00,000/ (SCCH12) 13 MVC No.217/2022 for pain and sufferings when right leg was amputed and disability was 70%.

entities.text: Mohd Sabeer @ Shabir Hussain V/s Regional Manager U.P State Road Transport Corporation, Civil Appeal No.9070 9071 of 2022
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The same can be applied to the present case also in the opinion of this court.
Therefore, for pain and suffering the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.2,00,000/ .
Accordingly same is awarded.
(ii) For Medical expenses:
The petitioner has produced medical bills at Ex.P.11 and prescriptions at Ex.P.12.
They show that, he has spent Rs.58,448/ because of the accident.
In the cross examination of P.W.1 those medical bills are disputed, but no satisfactory material is forthcoming to disbelieve the bills.
Petitioner stated that he has spent Rs.1,95,000/ for medical treatment.
But he has produced bills only for Rs.58,448/.
He is entitled for the said bill amount only.
Accordingly, it is held that petitioner is entitled for Rs.58,448/ towards medical expenses.

Basavegowda vs Rakshith A.R on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104850421/
6 (iii)
For Food and nourishment:
The petitioner was in hospital for one month.
Accident took place in the year 2021.
Since he was in hospital, food and nourishment charges will have to be awarded.
Considering the cost of living, and food, nourishment charges if per day Rs.300/ is awarded it will meet the ends of justice.
Hence for food and nourishment Rs.300/ x 31 days = Rs.9,300/is awarded.
(iv) For Attendant charges: For a period of inpatient for one month, someone should have looked after petitioner in the hospital.

Even if his family member has taken care of him in the said period,
that family member's income for those days is lost.
(SCCH12) 14 MVC No.217/2022 Hence attendant charges has to be awarded.

if per day Rs.300/
is awarded as attendant charges in 2021, it will meet the ends of justice.
Hence for attendant charges Rs.300/ x 31 days =Rs.9,300/is awarded.
(v) For Loss of income during laid up period: As per the finding to issue No.2, the income of the petitioner per month is Rs.14,000/.
He was inpatient for 31 days and he was advised to take rest also as he has underwent operation.
Minimum 6 months is required to recover from such operation in view of grievous injury and his old age.
Therefore, laid up period of petitioner is considered as total 6 months including in patient period of one month and loss of income during laid up period is Rs.14,000/x 6 = 84,000/.
He is entitled to Rs.84,000/ as loss of income during laid up period.
(vi) Conveyance charges: It is stated that petitioner was shifted to hospital from the spot of accident.
He took treatment at Adichunchanagiri hospital, Nagamangala Taluk, Mandya District and also spent money for conveyance.
Considering all those conveyances, in the opinion of this tribunal if an amount of Rs.10,000/ is awarded it will meet the ends of justice.
(vii) Loss of future income due to Disability : As per the findings given to issue no.2 functional disability of the petitioner is assessed at the rate of 70%.
Therefore, loss of future income due to disability is calculated as Rs.14,000X12 months X 70% disability X 9 multiplier to the age group above 5660 years = Rs.10,58,400/.
Hence, in the opinion of this court, petitioner (SCCH12) 15 MVC No.217/2022 is entitled for a sum of Rs.10,58,400/ towards loss of future income due to disability.
(viii) Physical discomfort and loss of amenities of life : As per the evidence of doctor, petitioner cannot walk properly, suffers pain and discomfort.
Meaning, he cannot lead the normal life as he used to live before the accident.
Certainly accident has caused physical discomfort and came in the way of normal enjoyment of life of petitioner.
Hence in the opinion of this court, petitioner is entitled to compensation under the head of physical discomfort and loss of amenities of life.

Under the said head he is entitled for Rs.20,000/.
(ix)
For Future medical expenses: P.W.2 has mentioned that for artificial leg cost varies from Rs.60,000/ to 2 lakhs.
He has not submitted any estimation report in that regard.
Petitioner also not submitted any estimation from the expert in respect of artificial leg fixation.
However, petitioner will be in need of future medical treatment in respect of his injury.

Therefore in the opinion of this Basavegowda vs Rakshith A.R on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104850421/
7 court, the expenses towards future medical treatment shall be awarded @ Rs.80,000/ to the petitioner.

sentences.text:
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for compensation as follows: Particulars of Heads In Rs.
i.

Pain & Sufferings 2,00,000/
ii.

Medical expenses 58,488/
iii. Food and nourishment 9,300/
iv.

Attendant charges 9,300/
v. Loss of income during laid up 84,000/
 (SCCH12) 16 MVC No.217/2022  period vi.

Conveyance charges 10,000/
vii. Loss of income due to disability 10,58,400/
viii Physical discomfort and loss of 20,000/
 amenities of life
ix. Future medical expenses 80,000/
Therefore, I hold that the petitioner is entitled for a total compensation of Rs.15,29,488/ in respect of injuries sustained by him in the Road traffic accident.
17. Liability:
Since respondent no.2 has admitted the insurance policy of two wheeler bearing No.KA01HW5028 which is valid on the date of accident, respondent no.2 is liable to indemnify the insured.
In view of settled law on the point of interest, though petitioner claimed interest at the rate of 12% pa he is only entitled to 6% interest on the award amount except on future medical expenses.

Hence, I answer this issue "Partly in the Affirmative".
18. ISSUE NO.5:

In view of above reasons I proceed to pass following :
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner u/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with costs.
(SCCH12) 17 MVC No.217/2022 It is held that, petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.15,29,488/ with interest @ 6% pa on the said from the date of petition till the date of payment.

Basavegowda vs Rakshith A.R on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104850421/
8
The 2nd respondent is liable to indemnify the insured and 2nd respondent is directed to deposit the aforesaid compensation amount with interest within two months from the date of this order.

After such deposit, the petitioner is entitled to have release of 50% of entire compensation in his favour and remaining 50% of the compensation shall be kept in F.D in any nationalized bank of the choice of the petitioner for a period of 5 years and he is entitled to receive periodical interest.

The Advocate fee is fixed at  Rs.1,000/.
 Award be drawn accordingly.
